lines: Oh! A visitor. Come in, come in. Mind the rug, it's older than I am, and that's saying something.
I'm the Seer. I watch the stars from up here, and I look into this old lantern of mine.
{player}: What do you see in it?
Swirls, mostly. But swirls can tell you a lot, if you're patient. Little hints of what's next.
And this is Hoot. He's meant to keep watch with me. He's asleep. He's always asleep.
(Hoot opens one eye, looks you up and down, and shuts it again.)
That round table is where the Council meets: a few of us who watch the stars and try to see what's coming, so we can help when help's needed.
We can't see everything, mind. The future's shy. It only ever peeks.
Come and see me whenever you like, and I'll read the lantern for you. It's very good at telling you what's next, and hopeless at telling you anything else.

rotate: The Wizard Lizard? Oh, he's a dear old friend. He's the principal up at the castle school these days.
He comes round for tea after our Council meetings and falls asleep in my armchair. Every time.
See that chart? The one that looks like a teapot? I named it the Teapot. Nobody else calls it that. Yet.
My granny used to say every star up there was somebody's wish once. I don't know if it's true. I like it, though.
The Council's chairs are empty more often than not. Looking into the future is tiring work. There are a lot of naps.
(Hoot says nothing at all. He's asleep.)
Well. I can tell he means it.
When the whole town's asleep, the stars talk a little louder. That's the best time to listen.

lines: Ah, {player}. Sit, sit, the kettle's always on. Let's see what the lantern has to say.
